caveats: **The walk refuses a few writes that are not redirects.** An ancestor the agent may traverse but not read (`access_denied`), an ordinary ancestor that holds a value named `SymbolicLinkValue` (`key_is_link`) and a path whose case differs from the stored spelling outside ASCII (`key_is_link`) are refused by the walk; on `HKLM` and `HKU` the fast open accepts the first two, and the write lands on the real key. `HKCR` can be refused `key_is_link` where its merged view puts a lower component in the other backing hive than the first (measured on Windows 11, 2026-10-23, for an interactive user; as SYSTEM, `HKCR` shows only `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes`), and for a real user `HKCU\Software\Classes` is itself a link (measured 2026-10-25), so a creating write below it is refused. Write such keys under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes` or `HKU\<SID>_Classes` directly; an `HKCR` write that succeeds lands in the backing hive while its audit row says `HKCR`.

**The audit trail identifies a change but cannot always reproduce it, and it can hold secrets.** Names are folded for the line (`audit_token`: space, `=`, `,`, `|`, control characters, the C1 controls, U+2028, U+2029 and a trailing backslash become `_`, cut at 256 bytes), old and new data are raw hex cut at 256 bytes, a `delete_key` row carries counts and no values, and a dry run mints `result=success` rows with `dry_run=1`; the hex can hold a registry secret (owner risk acceptance, 2026-10-20: masking is planned and nothing redacts it today, see **Sensitivity.**). An exception inside a write is contained at the plugin boundary and leaves a fixed `result=failed`, `reason=exception` line with every other field `-` (for `apply`, `op=apply`, after the rows of the items already done), while an agent that dies mid-command leaves no row at all, so in both cases read the key back.

**Registry 2.0.0 and later ask a key for more access than 1.0.0 did.** `set_value` opens the leaf with `KEY_SET_VALUE` and `KEY_QUERY_VALUE` and creates under each parent with `KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY`, `delete_value` asks the same two on the leaf, `delete_key` asks `DELETE`, `KEY_ENUMERATE_SUB_KEYS` and `KEY_QUERY_VALUE`, and the walk adds `KEY_QUERY_VALUE` on every component; an ACL that grants less answers `access_denied`. A key the plugin creates is created with `DELETE` access, so that a stopped walk can remove it by handle: where an inherited ACL gives the agent identity no `DELETE` on a new key the create answers `access_denied`, deliberately with no retry.

**The offline per-user arm and `apply` have limits of their own.** The offline mount runs under one process-wide lock (a long write delays every other offline hive reader), its post-unload probe sees a hive loaded after the write returned but not a logon that failed while it was mounted, and a mount that fails to unload (`hive_unload_failed`), or one left by an agent that died mid-write, stays until `reg unload` or a reboot: the user's next logon can get a temporary profile, and the plugin neither retries the unload nor sweeps old mounts (#5292, #3140). `apply` is `HKLM` only and not transactional, its dry run cannot see the ACL a key that does not exist yet will inherit (so `would_apply` is a prediction for a missing key and a fact for an existing one), each `delete_key` item can vet up to 10,000 values with no deadline, and a 256-item plan mints up to 256 of the 600 `registry.write` rows an agent may write per minute. Keys that differ only in non-ASCII case are not recognised as one key by `dependent_items` or by the per-key handle map, so such a plan opens the key twice.

**Read output is display text, not exact bytes.** In every registry string a read renders, `|`, control characters other than TAB, DEL, the C1 controls, U+2028 and U+2029 become `_` and trailing NULs are dropped, so `a<U+2028>b`, `a<VT>b` and `a_b` render alike, and `get_value` has no exact-bytes mode for a string value; `get_user_value` reads a string value up to its first NUL and decodes `REG_MULTI_SZ` and `REG_LINK`, which `get_value` and `enumerate_values` leave as hex, and `enumerate_values` writes `value|<name>|<type>` with `value` as a literal tag, not a column. Do not drop the `ReturnLength` argument of the `AdjustTokenPrivileges` call in `PrivilegeScope` (`agents/shared/win_profiles.hpp`): without it the offline fallback silently never enabled its privileges until #2771. The `get_user_value` capture exercised the live-hive path, not the offline mount.

definitions.description: Apply a declarative plan of machine-hive (HKLM) changes -- set_value, delete_value, create_key and non-recursive delete_key items -- with a dry run, read-back verification of value writes and deletes (a created key is evidenced by its create disposition, an existing one by being opened) and an undo manifest in the response; nothing is persisted on the endpoint. Dry run is the default: pass dry_run=false to change anything. Each key is opened ONCE on a checked handle (a registry symbolic link is refused, never followed) and every item on it reuses that handle; the previous value is captured before it is changed, and an item whose previous value this plugin could not write back (a type it cannot write, a shape it would refuse) is refused before anything changes. A dry run and a real run take ONE verdict function over the same facts, so they agree item for item (would_apply or applied, or refused); a plan is refused whole as dependent_items when two items touch the same value or a key item overlaps another item's key. The dry run opens with the mutation's own access mask and checks create access on the deepest existing key, but it cannot see the ACL a key that does not exist yet will inherit: a real run can still be refused or fail where the dry run said would_apply (the keys it made are rolled back by handle and `created` reports any that stayed). NOT transactional: with continue_on_error=false the first refused or failed item stops the run and the rest are skipped; the exit code is non-zero whenever any item was refused or failed. THE EXACT-NAME RULE: every key path and value name the manifest carries must read back as exactly what is in the registry, so a name that a row cannot spell (a `|`, a control character, a C1 control, U+2028 or U+2029, invalid UTF-8, a trailing backslash, or a value named `-`, which a row uses for the default value) is refused as unrepresentable_name before anything is changed, including the name of any value of a key an item would delete, whose raw UTF-16 name must also be well-formed (a lone surrogate or a NUL has no exact UTF-8 spelling and is refused the same way, in a dry run too; a value really named with U+FFFD is fine). Two value items on one key are also dependent_items whenever either name holds a non-ASCII character (Windows folds value-name case with a Unicode table the parser cannot reproduce). THE UNDO BUDGET: one 512 KiB budget charges every byte the manifest retains (previous values up to 4,096 bytes each, names and a fixed cost per row); a deleted key's values are all vetted but only as many as fit are returned, and when anything was cut the summary says undo_complete=0, in the dry run too, before anything is changed. THE UNDO CONTRACT: undo only `applied` items and `failed` ones with created above 0 or a mutation, in REVERSE item order; recreate a deleted key from its delete_key item (a key that held no values has no undo rows), then replay its undo rows in a second plan (a value whose name holds a non-ASCII character in a plan of its own when the key has other undo rows). The manifest restores VALUES only: a deleted key's owner, DACL, SACL, class and volatility are not captured, so a recreated key gets the parent's inherited security. It is a snapshot taken at capture: a value another writer changes between the capture and the change is lost or stale even with undo_complete=1. An item refused before its previous value was read shows "-" there, never "absent". Rows are written as each item concludes, so a later exception inside the plugin or a failed output channel cannot take back rows already written; the agent sends output at command end or each 64 KiB, so an agent that dies mid-plan loses whatever it had not sent (for a plan whose output is under 64 KiB, all of it): read the keys back with a dry run before replaying anything. The rows: one `audit` row per item that ran or was refused (recorded server-side as `registry.write`; a dry run's rows say dry_run=1 and record no change; three 256-item plans inside one minute exceed the server's 600 rows per agent per minute and the later rows are suppressed), its `item` row and, for a deleted key, its `undo` rows, then a closing `summary`. The plan parameter, with every value in it, is stored unredacted in the execution's parameter_values, and the reply holds previous values (secrets included) for Response:Read holders. Needs registry 2.1.0 on the agent: an agent at registry 1.x or 2.0.x answers `error|unknown action`. Windows-only.

Delete a Windows registry key. By default only a key with no subkeys is deleted (one with subkeys is refused as key_has_subkeys and nothing is deleted); `recursive` true removes the key and everything beneath it, and `dry_run` true counts what a real run would remove and deletes nothing. The key is opened on a checked handle (one canonical-name-checked open, with a component walk as the fallback) and a registry symbolic link in the path is refused, never followed (the key AT the path may itself be a link: the link object is removed and its target is untouched). A recursive delete first VETS the whole tree: every child is opened from its parent's handle with the delete's own access and probed for a link, and a link anywhere in the tree is refused as key_is_link with nothing deleted (a child whose ACL denies the delete, as access_denied, in a dry run too; a key whose raw UTF-16 name is not well-formed, which no UTF-8 name can open exactly, as unrepresentable_name). It then removes the tree post-order, each key by its own handle (no RegDeleteTreeW, which follows links), re-checking every key it finds for a link: a link planted since the vet stops the delete as key_is_link, and a tree that grew past the vet's bound stops it as concurrent_change, with what was already removed counted. The vet is a size bound and a link sweep, not a list of the keys it saw: a key added after it is deleted and counted like any other. It visits at most 10,000 keys and values and 600 levels; a dry run past that reports a lower bound with capped=1, and a real recursive delete of a tree it could not finish is refused as tree_too_large with nothing deleted (delete it in parts). On a dry run or a refusal the counts are what the vet counted; on a real run they are what the delete removed (exact when it succeeds, the partial total when it stopped), so they can exceed a dry run's. A non-recursive delete of a key holding more than 10,000 values removes only that key and its own values. MIXED FLEETS: an agent running registry 1.x or 2.0.x (every agent released before 2.1.0, v0.14.1 included) reads neither `recursive` nor `dry_run`: sent dry_run=true it DELETES a key that has no subkeys (a key with subkeys is refused), and a bare `status|ok` or a `dry_run|0` row in answer to dry_run=true means the key was deleted. The server does not compare plugin versions at dispatch (#6484), so upgrade the server, then the agents to registry 2.1.0 before using either flag, scope any preview to a tag that marks devices verified at 2.1.0, and until then use the delete_key kill switch as the stop-gap. Windows-only.

Delete a registry value from a specific user's hive; the key itself is left in place. Same profile resolution, live-or-offline hive path, hive-file guard, read-back verification, flush and audit row as set_user_value (the deleted value's previous data is in that row and in the response). Needs registry 2.1.0 on the agent: an agent at registry 1.x or 2.0.x answers `error|unknown action`. Windows-only.

Delete a specific value from a Windows registry key; the key itself is left in place. Registry 2.0.0 reports a failure as an `error|<token>` line (key_not_found, value_not_found, key_is_link, access_denied ...) instead of a sentence, limits the key path to 255 bytes and 32 components, and emits one leading `audit|op=delete_value|...` row (the old value, hex) before `status|ok`. Windows-only.
List all immediate subkeys under a registry key, one row per subkey. Windows-only.
List all value names and types under a Windows registry key, one row per value. Value data itself is not returned — use get_value to read a specific value. Windows-only.

Read a registry value from a specific user's registry hive. Resolves the target profile via ProfileList (by username or an explicit SID), then reads the live HKEY_USERS\<SID> hive if the user is logged in, or loads that profile's NTUSER.DAT via RegLoadKey as a fallback. SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege are required only for the offline fallback when the target user is not logged in; reading an already-loaded live hive needs no elevated privilege. Windows-only.

Read a value from the Windows registry. Value data is decoded for REG_SZ/REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_DWORD/REG_QWORD; every other type, including REG_MULTI_SZ and REG_LINK, is returned as hex-encoded bytes rather than decoded (get_user_value decodes both of those). Windows-only.
Check whether a registry key exists, without reading any of its values. Windows-only.

Enumerate local Windows user profiles from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList: SID, resolved profile name, profile path, and whether the profile's registry hive is currently loaded under HKEY_USERS. System profiles (LocalSystem, LocalService, NetworkService) are excluded. Windows-only.

Write a registry value into a specific user's hive. Resolves the target profile via ProfileList (by username or an explicit SID), then writes through the live HKEY_USERS\<SID> hive if the user is logged in, or loads that profile's NTUSER.DAT as a fallback. The offline load runs behind the shared hive-file guard (reparse ancestors, a second hard link, ownership, transaction-log sidecars and the file identity after the load are checked first), the write is verified by reading it back, and the key is flushed to disk before the hive unloads (a flush that fails fails the write). SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege are needed only for the offline fallback. A hive that is loaded after the write returned is reported as a warning; a logon that failed while the hive was mounted leaves no trace. Same types, encoding and verification as set_value. A `registry.write` audit row records the previous and new values (hex, capped at 256 bytes; they can contain secrets: the product owner accepted this risk on 2026-10-20 and masking is a planned later change), and the `value` and `data_hex` parameters are stored unredacted in the execution's parameter_values. Needs registry 2.1.0 on the agent: an agent at registry 1.x or 2.0.x answers `error|unknown action`. Windows-only.

Write a value to the Windows registry, creating missing key components beneath an existing top-level key (a path whose first component is missing is refused as root_level_create). All six writable types are supported (REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_BINARY, REG_DWORD, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_QWORD) and the write is verified: the previous value is captured first, the new one is read back on the same handle and compared byte for byte, and a mismatch fails the action. The key is opened on a checked handle (one canonical-name-checked open, with a component walk as the fallback) and a registry symbolic link anywhere in the path is refused, never followed; a write under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet, itself a link, therefore fails as key_is_link. The previous and new values are recorded in a `registry.write` audit row (hex, capped at 256 bytes; they can contain secrets: the product owner accepted this risk on 2026-10-20 and masking is a planned later change). Needs registry 2.0.0 on the agent: an agent still running registry 1.x writes an EMPTY REG_SZ for a data_hex-only write, stores REG_QWORD, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ and REG_BINARY values as REG_SZ text and follows a write under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet, all answering `status|ok`, so upgrade the agents first. Windows-only.

description: Windows Registry -- get, set (six types, verified), delete value, delete key (optionally recursive), enumerate, per-user reads and writes, bulk apply with an undo manifest
how_it_works:
> **Read this first: four facts that decide what a registry write does.**
>
> 1. **`HKCU` is the agent's own hive, not the logged-on user's.** The agent runs as LocalSystem, so `hive=HKCU` reaches `HKU\.DEFAULT`, LocalSystem's own profile hive. To read or change a person's settings use `get_user_value`, `set_user_value` or `delete_user_value` with their `sid` or `username` (`list_profiles` lists them), or `hive=HKU` with their SID as the first key component while their hive is loaded.
> 2. **Only `apply` previews by default.** `apply` is a dry run unless you send `dry_run=false`. `delete_key` deletes unless you send `dry_run=true`. `set_value`, `delete_value`, `set_user_value` and `delete_user_value` have no preview at all: they act at once.
> 3. **The undo manifest exists only in the reply.** Nothing is kept on the endpoint. Save the reply of every write to the change record when it arrives; the stored response is deleted after 90 days by default.
> 4. **Destructive actions need explicit targets.** `delete_value`, `delete_key`, `delete_user_value` and `apply` take explicit `agent_ids`; a scope or a broadcast is refused, for a dry run too. Every write, and `get_user_value`, also needs an administrator or an approval.

The plugin reads and changes the Windows registry on demand, in-process, with no scheduled collection. Six actions only read: `get_value`, `key_exists`, `enumerate_keys` and `enumerate_values` open one key of `HKLM`, `HKCU`, `HKCR` or `HKU`; `list_profiles` lists the machine's user profiles; `get_user_value` reads one value from a user's hive. Six actions change it: `set_value` and `delete_value` write or delete one value, `delete_key` deletes one key (with `recursive=true`, a whole tree), `set_user_value` and `delete_user_value` change one value in a user's hive, and `apply` runs a plan of up to 256 `HKLM` items with an undo manifest. Every change runs on a checked handle (the key is proven to be the one you named, never one reached through a registry link), is read back before it reports success, and writes one `audit|` line that the server turns into a `registry.write` audit row. A user's hive is the live `HKEY_USERS\<SID>` hive when it is loaded, otherwise the profile's `NTUSER.DAT`, mounted for the one call behind the hive-file guard and flushed before it is unloaded. The plugin keeps nothing on the endpoint and has no key policy of its own: the role, the approval, the per-action kill switch and the audit row are the controls. On macOS and Linux every action answers one `registry|unsupported|...` line.

inputs.description: A JSON array of up to 256 flat objects (64 KiB at most). Fields (all strings): `op` (set_value, delete_value, create_key or delete_key), `hive` (HKLM, the default and the only one), `key`, `name`, `type`, `value`, `data_hex`. set_value takes type (default REG_SZ) and value or data_hex, exactly as the set_value action; a present but empty `data_hex` is the zero-byte form (REG_BINARY only), which lets a captured empty value round-trip. delete_value takes key and name; create_key and delete_key take key only (delete_key is NOT recursive and refuses a link). A set_value or create_key item whose first key component does not already exist directly under the hive is refused root_level_create, in a dry run and a real run alike. An agent still on registry 1.x or 2.0.x answers `error|unknown action`.

inputs.description: "true" (the default) reports every item's verdict and changes nothing; "false" applies the plan. Any other spelling is refused as invalid_data (the direct command route, which has no enum, also accepts 1 and 0).
inputs.name: dry_run

inputs.description: "true" keeps applying later items after a refused or failed one; "false" (the default) stops and reports the remaining items skipped.

inputs.description: "true" deletes every subkey and value beneath the key as well; "false" (the default) refuses a key that has subkeys. The tree is vetted first (at most 10,000 keys and values and 600 levels, else tree_too_large with nothing deleted; a registry link inside it is refused as key_is_link), and the counts of a dry run are a snapshot. Any other spelling is refused as invalid_data (the direct command route, which has no enum, also accepts 1 and 0). Needs registry 2.1.0 on the agent: registry 1.x and 2.0.x ignore it.

Needs registry 2.1.0 on the agent: an agent at registry 1.x or 2.0.x ignores this flag and DELETES a key that has no subkeys, so upgrade agents first (docs/user-manual/upgrading.md).

Send exactly one of `value` and `data_hex`. When neither is sent, or the one sent is empty, the write stores an empty value of the type and answers ok: an empty string, the empty list or zero bytes (REG_DWORD and REG_QWORD refuse it as invalid_data), so a misspelt parameter name writes an empty value instead of failing. Through MCP `execute_instruction` and the result-set execute routes every parameter value is limited to 64 KiB.

inputs.description: The exact bytes to write, as hex, for any type; give it INSTEAD of `value` (both non-empty is refused as invalid_data). Shape is checked per type: 4 bytes for REG_DWORD, 8 for REG_QWORD, a terminating NUL for the string types, a trailing double NUL for REG_MULTI_SZ. Use it for exact bytes you hold from another source. An empty `data_hex` is the same as omitting it here. The plugin takes at most 1 MiB of data (2,097,152 hex characters), but MCP `execute_instruction` and the result-set execute routes limit every parameter value to 64 KiB, so through them it carries at most 32 KiB of data; the direct command route is not under that cap. Needs registry 2.0.0 on the agent: registry 1.x ignores it and writes an EMPTY REG_SZ over the value, answering `status|ok` (with type=REG_DWORD and data_hex only, 1.x throws and writes nothing).

columns.description: item and undo: the plan item index (0-based). audit: op=apply.<op>. summary: the item count.
columns.name: field_1

columns.description: item: the op (set_value, delete_value, create_key, delete_key). undo: the value name ("-" for the default value). audit: hive=. summary: items applied (or that would apply in a dry run).
columns.name: field_2

columns.description: item: the hive. undo: the value type. audit: result= (ok, refused, failed). summary: items refused.
columns.name: field_3

columns.description: item: the key path (exact for an item that proceeds). undo: the value data as hex (the kept bytes, then ~<total> when the capture was cut). audit: reason=. summary: items failed.
columns.name: field_4

columns.description: item: the value name ("-" for none or the default value; exact for an item that proceeds). undo: 1 when the capture was cut, else 0. audit: verify=. summary: items skipped after a stop.
columns.name: field_5

columns.description: item: the verdict (would_apply in a dry run, applied, refused, failed, skipped). audit: key= (capped at 256 bytes). summary: 1 for a dry run, 0 for a real run.
columns.name: field_6

columns.description: item: the refusal or failure token (key_not_found, value_not_found, key_has_subkeys, key_is_link, access_denied, root_level_create, tree_too_large, unsupported_old_type, unrepresentable_name, verify_mismatch, invalid_* ...) or "-". audit: name= (capped). summary: 1 when the undo manifest is complete, 0 when anything was cut or a creating item failed part-way.
columns.name: field_7

columns.description: item: the read-back verification (ok, mismatch, "-"). audit: type=.
columns.name: field_8

columns.description: item: the number of key components this item created (reverse: delete_key of each, deepest first), predicted in a dry run. audit: len=.
columns.name: field_9

columns.description: item: the previous value state (absent, present, unreadable) for value ops; "-" for a key op and for an item refused before its previous value was read (never read as absent). audit: dry_run=.
columns.name: field_10

columns.description: item: the previous value type. audit: counted_keys= ("-" for a delete_key that was invalid or whose open failed).
columns.name: field_11

columns.description: item: the previous value as hex (the kept bytes, then ~<total> when it was cut or the undo budget dropped it); restore it with data_hex. audit: counted_values=, or "-" when the item was refused before the contents of its key were read.
columns.name: field_12

columns.description: item: the new value length in bytes, or "-". audit: capped=, or "-" when not read. (The six audit tokens that follow -- created, sid, old_state, old_type, old, new -- are in the raw row and the registry.write audit row.)
columns.name: field_13

columns.description: Confirms the run succeeded and, on a real run, that the handle read back as deleted (a dry run answers ok too); only ever emitted on success — a failure is reported as an `error|<token>` line (not exhaustive: key_not_found, key_has_subkeys, tree_too_large, key_is_link, access_denied, verify_mismatch, concurrent_change, invalid_key_path, invalid_data or win32:<code>) and a non-zero exit instead of this column. A run that resolves its hive and key, success or not, also emits one `audit|op=delete_key|...` row (dry_run=1 on a dry run, whose success row records that a vet ran, not a deletion); a missing hive or key, or an unparseable hive, is a bare `error|...` line with nothing opened and no audit row. Values: ok.
columns.name: status

columns.description: Keys in the subtree, the target included: on a real run what the delete REMOVED (exact when it succeeds, the partial total when it stopped), on a dry run what the vet counted (a lower bound when capped is 1). A non-recursive delete counts the target alone, so 1. Emitted on success only: a refusal carries its counts in the audit row (counted_keys=). Values: a non-negative integer.
columns.name: counted_keys

columns.description: Values in those keys, counted the same way (a lower bound whenever capped is 1). Point in time: a writer racing the delete can add values a dry run never saw. Values: a non-negative integer.
columns.name: counted_values

columns.description: Whether this was a dry run: 1 (counted, nothing deleted) or 0 (a real run). Values: 1, 0 — a digit, never true/false.
columns.name: dry_run

columns.description: Whether the vet or the value enumeration stopped at its bound (10,000 keys and values, 600 levels), making the counts a lower bound; reported on a dry run or a non-recursive delete of a key holding more than 10,000 values (it removes that key with all its values). A real recursive delete past the bound is refused as tree_too_large, never capped: that refusal says capped=1 in its audit row only. Values: 1 (capped), 0 (complete) — a digit, never true/false.
columns.name: capped

columns.description: Confirms the delete was verified (and, on the offline NTUSER.DAT arm only, flushed with RegFlushKey before the unload; a live HKEY_USERS\<SID> delete is not flushed); only ever emitted on success — a failure is an `error|<token>` line (not exhaustive: value_not_found, key_not_found, hive_not_found, privilege_missing, hive_mount_failed, profile_list_unreadable, a hive-file guard token, flush_failed:<token>, access_denied or win32:<code>), preceded by the hive's own error sentence, and a non-zero exit. The same warnings as set_user_value may precede the audit row. A run whose profile resolves also emits one `audit|op=delete_user_value|...` row (hive=HKU, sid=<SID>); a missing sid, username or key, or a profile that is not found, is a bare `error|...` line with nothing opened and no audit row, while a key path or value name that fails shape validation after the profile resolved is audited as result=refused. Values: ok.
columns.name: status

columns.description: Confirms the delete succeeded; only ever emitted on success — a failure is reported as an `error|` line and a non-zero exit instead of this column. Values: ok.
columns.name: status

columns.description: One immediate subkey name under the given key; zero rows means the key has no subkeys. Display text (registry 2.0.1 and later): `|`, every control character except TAB, DEL, the C1 controls, U+2028 and U+2029 each become `_`, so two names that differ only there render alike. Values: free text.
columns.name: subkey

columns.description: The value's name; zero rows means the key has no values. Display text (registry 2.0.1 and later): `|`, every control character except TAB, DEL, the C1 controls, U+2028 and U+2029 each become `_`, so two names that differ only there render alike. Values: free text.
columns.name: name

columns.description: The value's registry type, named via the shared type table shared with get_value and get_user_value. Values: REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_DWORD, REG_QWORD, REG_BINARY, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_NONE, REG_LINK, REG_DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN, REG_UNKNOWN.
columns.name: type

columns.description: The resolved profile display name the value was read from — falls back to the caller's own username/sid input, then the resolved sid, but is never fabricated and never empty (ADR-0024 D11). Values: free text.
columns.name: username

columns.description: The value's data as a display string: a REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ or REG_LINK value is read up to its first NUL (as Windows reads it; get_value shows an interior NUL as `_`), REG_MULTI_SZ records are semicolon-joined and REG_LINK gives its target (get_value leaves those two hex-encoded). Display text, not exact: the characters get_value's value column folds become `_` here too (registry 2.0.1 and later). Values: free text.
columns.name: value

columns.description: The registry value type, named via the shared type table. Values: REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_DWORD, REG_QWORD, REG_BINARY, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_NONE, REG_LINK, REG_DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN, REG_UNKNOWN.
columns.name: type

columns.description: The value's data, decoded to a display string, for a value of at most 1 MiB (registry 2.0.1 and later; older agents read the whole value). Never truncated: a larger value fails the action with `error|value exceeds 1 MiB limit` rather than returning a partial string. Display text, not exact: `|`, every control character except TAB, DEL, the C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F), U+2028 and U+2029 each become `_` and trailing NULs are dropped, so those characters cannot be recovered from the row; get_value has no exact-bytes mode for a string value (the types it returns as hex are exact). Values: free text.
columns.name: value

columns.description: The registry value type, named via the shared type table shared with get_user_value and enumerate_values. Values: REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_DWORD, REG_QWORD, REG_BINARY, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_NONE, REG_LINK, REG_DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN, REG_UNKNOWN.
columns.name: type

columns.description: Whether the key could be opened for read. Values: true, false.
columns.name: exists

columns.description: The profile's Windows security identifier. Values: free text (a Windows SID string).
columns.name: sid

columns.description: The resolved profile folder name (the last path component of ProfileImagePath); rendered "-" when it cannot be resolved — never falls back to the sid (ADR-0024 D11). Values: free text or "-".
columns.name: profile_name

columns.description: The profile's ProfileImagePath, environment-expanded; rendered "-" when it is absent or unreadable. Values: free text or "-".
columns.name: profile_path

columns.description: Whether the profile's registry hive is reachable right now. Values: loaded, loaded_classes_only, not_loaded.
columns.name: hive_state

columns.description: Confirms the write was verified (and, on the offline NTUSER.DAT arm only, flushed with RegFlushKey before the unload; a live HKEY_USERS\<SID> write is not flushed); only ever emitted on success — a failure is an `error|<token>` line (not exhaustive: hive_not_found, privilege_missing, hive_mount_failed, profile_list_unreadable, a hive-file guard token such as hive_path_reparse_ancestor, flush_failed:<token>, or any set_value token), preceded by the hive's own error sentence, and a non-zero exit. A `warning|hive_unload_failed: ...`, `warning|hive_loaded_after_offline_write` or `warning|hive_post_unload_probe_failed:win32_<n>` line may precede the audit row. A run whose profile resolves also emits one `audit|op=set_user_value|...` row (hive=HKU, sid=<SID>); a missing sid, username or key, or a profile that is not found, is a bare `error|...` line with nothing opened and no audit row, while a key path or value name that fails shape validation after the profile resolved is audited as result=refused. Values: ok.
columns.name: status

columns.description: Confirms the write succeeded and read back identical; only ever emitted on success — a failure is reported as an `error|<token>` line (not exhaustive: access_denied, key_not_found, root_level_create, key_is_link, concurrent_change, invalid_type, invalid_data, value_overflow, invalid_key_path, invalid_value_name, verify_mismatch or win32:<code>) and a non-zero exit instead of this column. A run that resolves its hive and key, success or not, also emits one `audit|op=set_value|...` row carrying the previous and new values (hex, capped); a missing hive or key, or an unparseable hive, is a bare `error|...` line with nothing opened and no audit row, while a key path or value name that fails shape validation after the hive resolved (invalid_key_path, invalid_value_name) is audited as result=refused. Values: ok.
columns.name: status

outputs_note:
Each action has its own line shape; there is no uniform row. A line is `name|value` or a tagged row, split on `|`, and `-` inside an `audit|` line means "not applicable" (the read actions never use `-` as a placeholder).

| Action | On success | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| `get_value`, `get_user_value` | `value\|...` and `type\|...`; `get_user_value` writes `username\|...` first | one `error\|...` line, rc 1 |
| `key_exists` | `exists\|true` or `exists\|false` | `error\|...` only for a missing or unknown hive or key parameter |
| `enumerate_keys`, `enumerate_values` | one `subkey\|<name>` or `value\|<name>\|<type>` line each; no lines for an empty key | `error\|key not found`, rc 1 |
| `list_profiles` | one `<sid>\|<profile_name>\|<profile_path>\|<hive_state>` row per profile, with no prefix; then `warning\|profile_list_truncated at 512 entries` when the list was cut and `warning\|profile_path_unreadable for <n> profile(s)` when some profile paths could not be read; zero rows is a success | `error\|profile_list_unreadable`, rc 1 |
| `set_value`, `delete_value` | `audit\|...`, `status\|ok` | `audit\|...`, `error\|<token>`, rc 1 |
| `delete_key` | `audit\|...`, `status\|ok`, then `counted_keys`, `counted_values`, `dry_run` (1 or 0) and `capped` (1 when a bound was hit and the counts are a lower bound) | `audit\|...`, `error\|<token>`, rc 1 (the counts ride in the audit line) |
| `set_user_value`, `delete_user_value` | any `warning\|...` lines, `audit\|...` with `hive=HKU` and `sid=<SID>`, `status\|ok` | the hive's own error line when the hive was not reached, `audit\|...`, `error\|<token>`, rc 1 |
| `apply` | per item, as it ends: `audit\|...`, `item\|...` and, for a key it deleted, one `undo\|...` row per value; then `summary\|...` | the same, then `error\|partial_failure`, rc 1, when any item was refused or failed |

A request that fails before anything is opened (a missing or unknown hive, a missing key, a profile that is not found, a plan whose shape or flags are invalid) is one bare `error|...` line with no audit line; a key path or value name that fails validation after the target resolved is audited as `result=refused`. The `delete_key` counts are point in time: without `recursive` they are what the key held (`counted_keys|1`), with it what the delete removed, or on a dry run what the vet counted.

**How to read a result.**

| You see | It means |
|---|---|
| `result=ok` and `status\|ok` | the change was made and read back identical (for `delete_key`, the key reads back as deleted) |
| `result=ok` with `dry_run=1`, or an `item` verdict `would_apply` | a preview: nothing changed |
| `result=refused` and `error\|<token>` | nothing changed; any key the call created was removed again |
| `result=failed` | a change was attempted and may have landed: read the key back; `created` above 0 counts keys the call made that stayed ("A partial or failed create" under Where the data goes) |
| per-user `result=ok` with `reason=hive_unload_failed` | the write is durable, but the user's offline hive is still mounted: a `reg unload` is owed (token table) |
| an `error\|...` line with no audit line | refused before anything was opened |
| `status\|ok` with no `audit\|` line before it | a registry 1.x agent answered: read the value back ("Before you roll out") |
| an `apply` reply with no `summary` row | the reply ended early: trust the rows that arrived and read back the keys of the items with none |

The field grammar of every row is in the generated table below and in the integrator references after "Undoing a change".

privileges.grant: `HKLM` writes (`apply` included) need the service account in `Administrators`, which LocalSystem is. `HKCU` is the service account's own hive (`HKU\.DEFAULT` under LocalSystem) and needs no elevation; it is not a logged-on user's hive. The per-user actions use a loaded `HKU\<SID>` hive with no extra privilege; when it cannot be opened (normally: the user is not logged on) they mount the profile's `NTUSER.DAT`, which needs `SeBackupPrivilege` and `SeRestorePrivilege`, already granted to the service account and enabled on the process token only for the span of the mount. `list_profiles` needs no elevated privilege. `NtDeleteKey` and `NtQueryKey` (ntdll) need only `DELETE` on the key and a handle the caller already holds.
privileges.if_refused: reads: `error|key not found`, `error|value not found`, `error|value exceeds 1 MiB limit`, `error|value changed while reading ...` or `error|win32:<code>`; writes: the audit line, then `error|<token>` naming the cause (`access_denied` among them; every token is in the token table under "Reference for integrators: error tokens"); the per-user actions add `hive_not_found`, `privilege_missing`, `hive_mount_failed` or a hive-file guard token
privileges.measured: 2026-10-23, bare-metal, elevated interactive user: the nine registry 2.0.1 actions captured (`docs/samples/windows.txt`); the three 2.1.0 actions are `[not captured]` there. The write arms, the recursive delete, the per-user writes and `apply` run in `tests/unit/test_registry_write_local_dispatcher.cpp` and `tests/unit/test_registry_win_internals.cpp` on elevated Windows runs

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows/lines travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (90 days), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Audit log.** The server, not the plugin, writes the `registry.write` rows: it parses the `audit|` lines of a reply frame (`server/core/src/plugin_result_audit.hpp`) only when the agent stamped the frame with one of the six write actions and the frame's command id is one the server minted for a registry command, so a read action, or a line that merely starts with `audit|`, mints nothing. `result=ok` is recorded as `success`, `refused` and `failed` as `failure`, with the whole line in the row's detail. An agent older than the release that contains #6294 stamps no action and produces no rows (`docs/user-manual/upgrading.md`). Principal, retention and the join to the operator's row: `docs/user-manual/audit-log.md`.

**Where each copy lives.** The reply (its rows and audit lines) is in the ResponseStore for 90 days by default (`--response-retention-days`), and it is the only copy of an `apply` undo manifest (the `item` rows' old values and the `undo` rows, up to 4,096 bytes per value); the AuditStore keeps one `registry.write` row per audit line for 365 days by default (`--audit-retention-days`), with old and new values cut to 256 bytes of hex; `executions.parameter_values` keeps the request parameters (`value`, `data_hex`, the whole `plan`) and no pass prunes it; the endpoint keeps nothing.

**Agent log.** The plugin's own `spdlog` error lines (for example `registry: <action> raised an exception`) carry no command id: the plugin ABI hands a plugin no command identifier. Attribute a command through the response and audit rows above, which are joined on the command id.

**A partial or failed create.** A `set_value` row with `result=failed` and `created=<n>` above 0, an `error|exception` reply, or an agent that stopped in the middle of a command can leave keys the call made (and, for a write that landed, its value). Take the hive, key and value name from the request that dispatched the command, not from the audit row: the exception row has `hive=-|key=-|created=-`, and the `command.dispatch` row carries only `registry:set_value -> N agent(s)`. The request parameters are in `executions.parameter_values` of the execution that holds the row's `command_id` (join on it; the command-to-execution mapping is reaped after 24 hours, so the join can come back empty, and then only the dispatching script, workflow or schedule holds the request). A call creates only the trailing components of a path that did not exist, and a pre-existing empty parent looks exactly like a created one; the rollback goes leaf first, so the keys a failed call leaves are normally the shallowest of the ones it made, but when the leaf holds a value or key another party put there, the leaf is kept and every ancestor above it survives with it. Read the candidates with `key_exists`, `enumerate_values` and `enumerate_keys`, and remove a key with `delete_key` (leaf first, one call per key) only when this call's creation of it can be shown (for example an earlier `key_exists` for the path answered false) and it is empty; a key that holds a value you did not write is another party's and stays. For an exception whose audit line could not be written, and for an agent that died mid-command (it sends output at command end or each 64 KiB), there is no `registry.write` row: only the `command.dispatch` row and the stored response show the attempt. A recursive `delete_key` stopped that way can leave the tree partly deleted with no row at all: run it again as a dry run to see what is left, then for real. An `apply` stopped that way keeps the rows the agent had already sent; an item with no row may still have run, and a deleted key's manifest is whole only when its `undo` rows number its audit `counted_values`, so read the keys of those items back before replaying anything.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics: nothing here runs on a schedule; the plugin executes only when an operator or workflow dispatches one of its twelve definitions.

**Sensitivity.** The audit rows of every mutating action (`apply` and the per-user writes included) and the `set_value`/`delete_value`/`set_user_value`/`delete_user_value` responses carry registry data OLD and NEW (hex of the raw bytes, 256 bytes at most per value in an audit row, for every value type) and key paths; an `apply` reply also carries its undo manifest, the previous value of each value item and every value of each deleted key (up to 4,096 bytes per value and 512 KiB per reply), readable by `Response:Read` holders for 90 days. All of these can hold secrets that live in the registry (a service account's autologon password, a product key, an agent token). **Owner risk acceptance:** old and new values are recorded as raw hex and can contain secrets; the product owner accepted this risk on 2026-10-20 and masking is a planned later change, and nothing in the plugin redacts them today. A key path can name a person. `get_value`/`enumerate_values`/`get_user_value` can return arbitrary registry data, among it `RegisteredOwner`/`DigitalProductId` (a person's name and a device-specific product-key hash); `get_user_value`'s `username` and `list_profiles`' `profile_name`/`profile_path` (e.g. `jsmith`/`C:\Users\jsmith`) directly identify a person and their home directory. The readers are wider than the writers: `AuditLog:Read` and `Response:Read` (the Viewer, Operator, PlatformEngineer, ITServiceOwner and Administrator roles hold both; `Response:Read` is not floored while RBAC is off), the legacy `/events` stream (any authenticated non-service-scoped session) and MCP `query_audit_log`; the executions' `parameter_values` carries the write parameters unredacted: `value` and `data_hex` of `set_value` and `set_user_value`, and the whole `apply` `plan` with every value in it. By default audit rows are retained 365 days (`--audit-retention-days`) and the response store 90 days (`--response-retention-days`); the executions table is not in the server's retention settings and no pass prunes it, so `parameter_values` stays until the database is purged. Read-time redaction is not built.
**Siblings:** none. Guardian's own real-time registry-key watch (`guard_type: "registry"`) is an unrelated detection mechanism; this plugin is on-demand only, with no watch/trigger surface.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) -> `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) -> `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("windows.registry.get_value")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`; the audit rows: the audit log API filtered on `registry.write`.
